summary: A timber R-6 lookout on the Ochoco National Forest built in 1964 beside a site used since 1918 or 1919; the register and firelookout.com date the first platform differently.

facts.design: 20-ft timber tower with a 14 x 14 ft flat-topped live-in R-6 cab and catwalk

access.note: Active staffed lookout. The sources read do not say whether visitors may go up into the cab. A 2011 visitor drove up by road.

visit.trail_note: Road 2630 is the access road. A 2011 visitor described it as rough and took 30 minutes to drive 6.2 miles.

events.note: First 10-ft platform on the summit. Firelookout.com and the 2011 blog give 1918; the register gives 1919
35-ft platform with a cabin (open platform with ground cabin per the register)
20-ft L-4 tower or cab; served 31 years until the present lookout was built
Present 20-ft R-6 timber tower built right beside the old tower, which was then removed
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register
Patrol point one mile north of the lookout burned in a 2008 forest fire; the lookout itself is not described as burned

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com and the 2011 blog give 1918 for the first 10-ft platform. The register gives 1919. The story reports both; the 1964 tower date is agreed by all three pages.

sources.title: Mt. Pisgah, Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: The 1964 build year and the 1923/1929/1933 sequence agree across sources. Staffing is from undated firelookout.com text and an undated register line; the only access report is a 2011 blog visit, so current road and cab-access status is unverified. Design wording differs slightly (NHLR says wooden; firelookout.com says treated timber), and both were kept as timber. Elevation is 6,800 ft per NHLR and 6816 ft per firelookout.com. The 2008 burn was a patrol point, not the lookout. Not read: the Ochoco National Forest pages and the Facebook FFLA post.
